entities.name: Wenceslaus II of Legnica
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Wenceslaus II, a prominent Silesian Piast duke, navigated the complex political and ecclesiastical landscape of late medieval Central Europe, serving as Duke of Legnica from 1364 until 1413, Bishop of Lebus (1375–1382), and then the highly influential Prince-Bishop of Breslau (Wrocław) from 1382 until 1417. Born around 1348, his life concluded on January 8, 1420. Holding significant temporal power as Duke of Nysa-Otmuchów, his career exemplifies the intertwined secular and spiritual authority characteristic of the Holy Roman Empire's eastern marches, particularly within the Kingdom of Bohemia, during a period of increasing Habsburg influence and the initial stirrings of the Hussite Wars.

Wenceslaus initially co-ruled Legnica with his brother Rupert I following their father Wenceslaus I's death, but soon pursued an ecclesiastical career, likely due to the limited family inheritance. He became Provost of the Collegiate Church of the Holy Cross in Wrocław by 1373. His elevation to Bishop of Lebus in 1375 placed him in a strategically important, though often impoverished, diocese. In 1382, he was transferred to the far wealthier and more influential Bishopric of Breslau, a move confirmed by Pope Urban VI. As Prince-Bishop, he wielded considerable temporal power over the Duchy of Nysa-Otmuchów, maintaining a complex relationship with the Bohemian crown and the local Silesian nobility. He resigned from the Bishopric in 1417, transferring it to his nephew Konrad IV, possibly due to advanced age or political pressures related to the escalating Hussite tensions.
